title: rebar shared sub-schemas
description: Reusable $defs referenced by the per-output rebar schemas. Authored once here and $ref'd everywhere (a {path,reason} entry, a dep, a comment, etc.) so the shapes never drift between, e.g., `get-file-impact` and `TicketState.file_impact[]`. Load schemas via rebar.schemas.validator(name), which wires a referencing Registry so these cross-file $refs resolve.

creation_channel.description: The public ingress that produced a ticket's genesis CREATE event: `cli` (the rebar CLI), `mcp` (the MCP server), `python` (the direct library facade), `jira` (Jira-inbound), `import` (NDJSON import), or `unknown` (a legacy CREATE that carried no channel; projection-only, never a valid live-write value).

close_class.description: The bounded classification recorded when a ticket is closed with `--class <value>` (REQUIRED for `bug` closes; on non-bug tickets only the administrative dispositions `duplicate`/`obsolete`/`superseded`/`wontfix` are accepted), folded into reduced state as `close_class`. One of: `regression` (a change reintroduced a previously-fixed defect), `plan_defect` (the design/plan was wrong), `env_integration` (an environment/integration issue), `flaky` (a nondeterministic/intermittent failure), `preexisting` (a latent defect that predated the work), `not_a_bug` (behaved as intended; bug-only), `duplicate` (already tracked elsewhere), `escalated` (handed off to the user/another owner; bug-only), `obsolete` (the premise no longer holds; requires a reason), `superseded` (replaced by a named live ticket), `wontfix` (a deliberate decision not to do the work; requires a reason), or `undetermined` (the escape hatch when no class fits).

completion_expectation.description: WHY a completion signature was or was not EXPECTED for a close — the write-time provenance stamped on the `*->closed` STATUS event in the same locked write as the close (never the signing outcome: the STATUS commits before signing is attempted). One of: `required` (gate on, verifier PASS, a signature was expected — `required` with no completion-verifier attestation reads as a signature-append failure), `disposition` (an administrative disposition close, signed as a DISPOSITION rather than a completion PASS), `gate_off` (the completion-verification close gate was genuinely configured off), `gate_unreadable` (the config could not be read; the fail-open skip is a fault, distinct from the `gate_off` policy choice), `force_bypassed` (an ENABLED gate was bypassed with `--force`; a forced close under a disabled/unreadable config records the gate state instead, the reason staying in `force_close_reason`), `local_source` (an opt-in local, unattested verdict — never signed), `not_certifiable` (verifier PASS but certification withheld, e.g. an uncertified force-closed descendant), or `not_applicable` (`idea -> closed`: a reject/drop, not a completion). Absent on a historical close event means unknown/legacy — never guessed.

source_author.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): original comment author from the source store. Present only on imported comments.

source_created_at.description: Provenance (P1.2 import): original comment timestamp from the source store. Present only on imported comments.

input.description: The raw input that failed to resolve.

exit_code.description: Optional: the process exit code that accompanied this failure (see docs/exit-codes.md). Present on emitted failure envelopes; omitted by legacy read-not-found callers.

severity.description: Finding severity, highest→lowest. 'info' is a non-actionable observation.

citation.description: Evidence backing a finding (rebar.llm). The `kind` discriminator selects the shape: a repo file location (path [, line_start, line_end]); a URL; or a freeform source/evidence description. `kind` is required so consumers can branch; the other fields are populated per kind.

line_end.description: 1-based end line (kind=file); 0/omitted means whole file (i.e. through the end).

description.description: Freeform source/evidence description (kind=source), or extra context for any kind.

finding.description: One reviewer finding — the universal output element of every LLM review operation (rebar.llm).

dimension.description: Category/dimension the finding belongs to (e.g. 'security', 'acceptance-criteria', 'test-coverage'). Reviewer-defined.

reviewer_id.description: Id of the reviewer prompt that produced this finding.
